Application Materials.content:
LSE carefully considers each application and takes into account all the information included on your application form, such as your:
- academic achievement (including predicted and achieved grades)
- statement of academic purpose
- two academic references
- CV
[See further information on supporting documents](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/Prospective-students/Supporting-documents).

Interview Requirements.content: We do not interview for places on the degree.

Application Deadlines.content:
Academic year 2026/27 start date: **28 September 2026**.
Application deadline: **None – rolling admissions.** Applications for this programme are considered on a rolling basis and will close once the programme is full. There is no fixed deadline.
For funding consideration, you must submit your application and all supporting documents by the relevant funding deadline:
- Funding deadline for needs-based awards from LSE: **23 April 2026**.
- Funding deadline for ESRC funding: **14 January 2026**.

Academic Requirements.content:
An **upper second class honours (2:1) degree in a relevant discipline (or equivalent)** is required. Students should normally have taken university courses including **calculus, linear algebra, and statistics**. Appropriate work experience will also be considered.
Linear algebra plays a major role in several key courses and in the field of OR generally. It is expected that students are comfortable with the basic notions: **linear independence, rank, determinants, solutions of systems of equations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors**; these will not be reviewed in the course.
For applicants from China: to be considered for admission to a taught master's programme requiring an **upper second class equivalent**, LSE would normally require a **bachelor's degree with an overall mark of 85 per cent** from applicants who have attended a highly regarded institution in China, while all other applicants are normally required to obtain a mark of **at least 90 per cent**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
The English language requirement for MSc Operations Research and Analytics is **Standard**. English tests must be **less than two years old by 1 October** of your start year. These are **minimum** requirements; selectors may require a higher score at their discretion. Additional language instruction (Presessional/Insessional) may be needed before registration.
| Test | Overall | Reading | Listening | Writing | Speaking |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| IELTS (Academic) | **7.0** | 6.5 | 6.5 | 6.5 | 6.5 |
| LSE Presessional | **70** | 65 | 65 | 65 | 65 |
| PTEA (in-person) | **70** | 62 | 62 | 62 | 62 |
| Cambridge English Scale | **185** | 176 | 176 | 176 | 176 |
| TOEFL iBT | **100** | 23 | 22 | 24 | 22 |
| TOEFL iBT (updated scale) | **5.5** | 5 | 5 | 5 | 4.5 |
| Trinity ISE | **Level III** | Merit | Merit | Merit | Merit |
Test notes: IELTS must be IELTS *Academic* (not General); online version accepted. PTEA is accepted **in-person only** (online not accepted). For Cambridge, for older tests, an online converter is used; C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency preferred. [Read more about LSE English language requirements](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/Prospective-students/Entry-requirements/English-language-requirements).

Program Overview.content:
MSc Operations Research and Analytics is a Graduate (Taught) programme in the Department of Mathematics. It is available full-time for 12 months for Home and Overseas students, with a start date of 28 September 2026 and location at Houghton Street, London.
This programme is designed for students wishing to deepen and broaden their mathematics knowledge, and gain skills in high demand in the marketplace. With study in practice and theory, students gain insight into analytics problems faced by businesses, governments, and nonprofits. On the practical side, students learn how to model real-world problems using optimisation, stochastic simulation, and machine learning, using specialist software taught in tutorial sessions. On the theoretical side, students learn to recognise canonical underlying mathematical problems and solve them with state-of-the-art methods. Courses are taught by faculty members with world-leading research profiles.
In the first term, students learn the fundamentals of operations research and machine learning. In the second term, they can choose from a range of courses in mathematics, statistics, finance, and management. Students undertake a final project where, working in a consultancy role and using the tools learned in the degree, they tackle a real problem faced by a partner organisation. Past and present partners include Amazon, BT, British Airways, Emirates Airlines, FICO, Ford Motor Company, Just Eat, Legal and General, the National Audit Office, and Transport for London. As an alternative to the project, more theoretically minded students can write a dissertation supervised by a faculty member.
The programme takes three compulsory courses and options within the Department and across other relevant departments, including Management and Statistics. During the summer, students are required to do either a project in Operations Research and Analytics or a Dissertation in Operations Research and Analytics. The project involves work in a host organisation in business, government, health, or a social non-profit organisation, in a consultancy role, typically turning a real problem faced by the organisation into a mathematical model whose solution provides tangible benefit. The dissertation requires study of an area of research, or an application of advanced techniques, and a report of findings.
Teaching combines traditional lectures with seminars. Several courses, including all three compulsory ones, involve using a programming language or specialised computational tools. Students develop these skills in a pre-sessional Python course and in the respective courses' seminars. Within the programme students take courses, including half unit courses and full unit courses, to a total of four units.
2024 admissions data: 290 applications, 24 intake, 12:1 ratio.
Student perspectives describe the programme as balancing theoretical foundations and industry applications, offering flexibility in course choice, and providing networking opportunities. One MSc Operations Research and Analytics student said the programme allowed study of topics such as combinatorial optimisation, advanced statistics, and algorithmic techniques for data mining.
The Department of Mathematics aims to be a leading centre for the study of mathematics in the social sciences. Its research encompasses four main overlapping areas: discrete mathematics; mathematical game theory; financial and related mathematics; and optimisation and algorithms. All aspects of its research were ranked world-leading or internationally excellent in the most recent [Research Excellence Framework (2021)](https://results2021.ref.ac.uk/profiles/institutions/10004063), submitted jointly with the Department of Statistics. The department offers three postgraduate programmes and has close ties with other departments at LSE, including Statistics, Economics, Finance, Management and the Data Science Institute.
This programme is ideal preparation for a range of careers in quantitative positions in consultancy, management, finance, government and business, anywhere in the world. Recent graduate placements include: Consultancy: Accenture, BCG, Deloitte, EY, PwC, McKinsey, Bain & Company, Decision Point Analytics, LET Consulting, and Turner & Townsend. Government: Ofgem and Ministry of Defence (Singapore). Business: Ali Baba, BMW group, BT group, Dish Network, Johnson & Johnson, Just Eat, Procter & Gamble, Renault group, Ocado, Red Bull, and Samba TV. Transportation: Airbus, British Airways, DiDi, Emirates, Laskarides Shipping, and Ryanair. Tech: Amazon, Ant Group, BT group, China Telecom Europe, Databricks, Flexciton, Huawei, Satalia, and Yahoo Japan. Banking and finance: Central Bank of the Bahamas, CiBanco, Citi, Credit Suisse, CITIC Securities, FinTru, Jane Street Capital, Guodu Securities, Point72 Asset Management, Shanghai Pudong Development Bank, and UBS. PhD study: Goethe University Frankfurt, Imperial College London, Monash University Malaysia, National University of Singapore, and University of Warwick.
Top 5 sectors students work in: Financial and Professional Services; Information, Digital Technology and Data; FMCG, Manufacturing and Retail; Insurance; Other Professional, Scientific and Technical Activities.

Curriculum.content:
Study mode / programme availability: Home full-time students (**12 months**) and Overseas full-time students (**12 months**). Start date: 28 September 2026. Location: Houghton Street, London.
In the first term, students learn the fundamentals of operations research and machine learning. In the second term, students can choose from a range of courses in mathematics, statistics, finance, and management. Course topics include algorithms and computation, optimisation, game theory, and further topics in machine learning and AI.
Programme content: students take three compulsory courses and choose courses from a range of options within the Department and across other relevant departments, including Management and Statistics.
Year 1:
- MA423 Half unit: [Optimisation Theory and Modelling](https://www.lse.ac.uk/resources/calendar/courseGuides/MA/2024_MA423.htm)
- MA424 Half unit: [Stochastic Modelling and Simulation](https://www.lse.ac.uk/resources/calendar/courseGuides/MA/2024_MA424.htm)
- MA429 Half unit: [Algorithmic Techniques in Machine Learning](https://www.lse.ac.uk/resources/calendar/courseGuides/MA/2024_MA429.htm)
- Choose one of these two courses: MA425 One unit [Project in Operations Research and Analytics](https://www.lse.ac.uk/resources/calendar/courseGuides/MA/2023_MA425.htm) or MA426 One unit [Dissertation in Operations Research and Analytics](https://www.lse.ac.uk/resources/calendar/courseGuides/MA/2023_MA426.htm)
- [Courses to the value of one and a half units from a range of options](https://www.lse.ac.uk/resources/calendar/programmeRegulations/taughtMasters/2025/MScOperationsResearch&Analytics.htm)
During the summer, students are required to do either a project in Operations Research and Analytics or a Dissertation in Operations Research and Analytics. The project involves work in a host organisation, in business, government, health, or a social non-profit organisation, in a consultancy role, typically turning a real problem faced by the organisation into a mathematical model whose solution provides tangible benefit; students are marked on a project report. The dissertation requires study of an area of research, or an application of advanced techniques, and a report of findings.
Within the programme students take a number of courses, including half unit courses and full unit courses, to a total of **four units**. In half unit courses, on average, students can expect **35 contact hours** in total and for full unit courses, **40-60 contact hours** in total. Teaching combines traditional lectures with seminars; several courses, including all three compulsory ones, involve using a programming language or specialised computational tools. Students develop these skills in a pre-sessional Python course and in the respective courses' seminars.

Cost of Attendance.content:
LSE broadly estimates that students should allow **£1,550 per month** for all living expenses, including accommodation, travel, food, laundry, study costs, and other personal expenses. This will vary depending on lifestyle and requirements.
- If you're an overseas student and require a student visa, you must ensure that you have sufficient funds for the first year of tuition fees and **up to nine months of living costs**, and provide evidence of these funds.
- Private housing costs in London can vary considerably depending on location and accommodation type, but start at approximately **£650 per month**.
- LSE estimates that students will spend **£150-£300 per month on food**, depending on whether they live in catered or self-catered halls, or in private accommodation.

Financial Aid.content:
Applications for this programme are considered on a rolling basis; however, if you’d like to be considered for any funding opportunities, you must submit your application and all supporting documents by the funding deadline.
- **Fee reduction:** Students who have completed and passed an undergraduate degree at LSE and are beginning taught graduate study at the School are eligible for a 10 per cent tuition fee reduction. Students who have completed and passed two or more Summer School courses are eligible for a five per cent reduction. If eligible for both discounts, the higher 10 per cent discount rate will apply. [Find out more about the LSE alumni discount](https://info.lse.ac.uk/staff/divisions/Finance-Division/Fees-Income-and-Credit-Control/Rewards-and-Discounts).
- **Scholarships and other funding:** LSE provides scholarships to help both home and overseas students. Some needs-based awards are offered for this programme, including the [Graduate Support Scheme](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding/secure/graduate-support-scheme). To apply for an award, you must have an offer of a place and submit a Graduate Financial Support application before the funding deadline. The funding deadline for needs-based awards from LSE is **23 April 2026**.
- In addition to needs-based awards, LSE offers [scholarships for students from specific regions of the world](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding) and [awards for certain subjects](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding/Department-or-programme-specific-funding). You can’t apply for a Graduate Support Scheme or LSE scholarship once you’ve joined the School.
- You can also apply for [Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC)](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding/ESRC-Studentships) funding when you apply as part of a 1+3 research programme. The 1+3 scheme provides funding for a one-year research training master's linked to a three-year PhD. To be considered for ESRC funding, you need to supply your application and any [supporting documents](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/Prospective-students/Supporting-documents) before the funding deadline. Funding deadline for ESRC funding: **14 January 2026**.
- LSE expects students who register for a programme to have sufficient funds for the duration.
- Learn more about [fees and funding opportunities](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding).

Multiple Applications.content:
You may submit an application via the online application system only ONCE within the application cycle (October 2025 to September 2026). When completing your initial online application, you may choose up to **two programmes** in order of preference. **If you are applying for two programmes, please submit a separate statement of academic purpose for each programme**. Your choices will be considered in sequence, and it is only possible to hold one offer of a place, so if you are offered a place on your first-choice programme you will not be considered for your second-choice unless you specifically request it.
If you are unsuccessful in your application to both of your initially chosen programmes and you wish to be considered for further, additional choices, you may do this by submitting the **Add/Amend programmes** form via the [Graduate Applicant Portal](https://lseportal.force.com/admissions/s/track-my-graduate-application) and paying an additional administrative fee of **£105**. You should not use this form to add choices 3 and 4 before receiving a decision on each of your original programme choices, unless you wish to withdraw your initial programme choices.
**You may only submit an application using the online application system ONCE in the same admissions cycle. If you submit a second online application within the same admissions cycle, it will not be considered.** **To apply to further programmes after you have submitted your initial online application, you must use the process above.**

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
LSE has a no-deferrals policy for offers for graduate programmes. The only exception to this is in cases of unforeseen illness or bereavement.
If your deferral is agreed in exceptional circumstances, LSE asks you to submit a deferral deposit as requested in your deferral letter, using the student self-funding [payment portal](https://portal.lse.ac.uk/payments/s/fees) to pay. The deposit must be received by the **January 31st deadline** to secure your new offer for next year. The deferral deposit is offset against your tuition fees once you register.
Your deposit may be refunded in exceptional circumstances, determined at the School's discretion. Documentary evidence of your inability to travel/attend your programme will be required. Examples of valid circumstances include: outbreak of war, refusal of Visa, inability to travel due to injury or illness, bereavement, and declining your offer before or on the **31 January deadline**. Circumstances where a refund would not be made include choosing to attend a different university and failure to secure funding.
If your circumstances match those above, you may request to defer your offer using the Extenuating Circumstances form on the Graduate Applicant Portal. If your request is agreed, your offer for the current year will be declined automatically, as you do not intend to come to LSE in this cycle.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
In order to take up your place you must fulfil the conditions that have been applied to your offer. These may include satisfying academic conditions, providing English language test results and/or degree results, or attendance at introductory or LSE Summer School courses. To fulfil the condition(s) you must send official documentary proof of your final degree mark or test scores, or attend the specified summer school or pre-sessional courses.
Introductory (pre-sessional) courses in mathematics and statistics are run in September for various courses - details are on your offer letter.
If you have failed to reach the standard of your conditions you should still send the official proof of your results. It may still be possible to confirm your offer - your results will be sent with your application file to the selector and a final decision will be made. If you have failed to attain the required language score by a large margin, you may arrange to re-take the test as long as you can submit the required score before the registration period begins.
If the selector has examined your degree results and your offer has not been confirmed, this decision is final - no appeal is possible. If your offer has been non-confirmed on the basis of your language test score you may arrange to re-take the test.
